Below that, one sentence — \"We made it to the raft.\" He read the words twice, then walked to his log and wrote them down, hands trembling not from cold but from the sudden, overwhelming knowledge that someone, somewhere, had survived long enough to hope a stranger would find this and understand. He kept the bottle on the windowsill for the rest of his life.", "w02": "凌晨四点，城市还没有完全睡着。路灯将橘黄色的光晕洒在湿漉漉的柏油路上，偶尔一辆出租车驶过，尾灯在夜色中画出一道红弧。便利店的霓虹灯忠实地亮着，收银台后的年轻人低着头，下巴快要碰到胸口。远处某栋高楼的一扇窗户透出白光，不知是谁彻夜未眠。环卫工人已经推着车出来了，扫帚划过地面发出沙沙声，像是城市在轻声耳语。空气里混着夜露与油烟的气味，安静得让人以为时间停住了，却又分明感觉到黎明正从某个看不见的地方，一点一点地靠近。", "w03": "• Recursion means a function calls itself to solve a smaller version of the same problem, like looking up a word in a dictionary only to find the definition uses another word you need to look up.\n• Every recursive function needs a \"base case\" — a simple situation where it just gives the answer directly without calling itself again, so it doesn't go on forever.\n• Think of it like nesting dolls: you open a doll to find a smaller doll, then a smaller one, until you reach the tiniest doll that doesn't open — that's your base case, and then you're done."}
